platform: Omarchy 4.0.4-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy, x86_64, Node v26.8.2
scope: Live desktop acceptance of the bar widget, the panel, the three store fetches, and the notification and link paths, re-run after the theme screenshots and hero swap, and again after the crops were re-cut to include the window border. Both of those commits change only README.md and images, so the runtime is byte-identical to e809ccf and the switch, bell and notification-click results carry over unchanged. Portable checks are separate and are listed for completeness.
install: Local checkout symlinked at ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/salmun-nister.loot-drops, already enabled in the bar's right section, then omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins. A plain directory is sufficient; no git remote was needed. The manifest, the bar-widget block and .template/project.json all carry the same description at this commit, so configure() no longer rewrites the repository description back to the old wording.
commands: omarchy-notification-send --app-name 'Loot Drops' -g '󰜦' -u normal -t 12000 '<headline>' '<body>' --exec omarchy-shell -q salmun-nister.loot-drops open

results.check: Bar widget loads on the real bar
results.detail: omarchy-shell shell listPlugins reports enabled:true for kinds ['bar-widget'], and shell debugBarGeometry places salmun-nister.loot-drops in the right section at x=2183, 27x25, visible:true and itemVisible:true. rescanPlugins reloaded it with no Loot Drops errors in the Quickshell log.

results.check: Panel opens and renders the three stores
results.detail: summon returned ok and mapped the omarchy-keyboard-panel layer. Captured from the live desktop: hero read 'Loot Drops' with the chest glyph over '4 FREE GAMES FROM STEAM, EPIC, AND GOG'; Steam listed Pony Island and Fireside Feelings; Epic Games listed Out of Sight and TerraScape; GOG showed its header row and nothing else; the footer held the refresh glyph, 'Updated 3m ago' and the ? button.

results.check: Empty store shows only its name
results.detail: GOG with no giveaway rendered a bare header row, keeping its bell and switch, with no empty-store line. Same behaviour as the previous run.

results.check: Hero is pinned and a fitting list does not scroll
results.detail: The offscreen harness against the three live stores reported rowCount 7, gameRows 4, headers steam/epic/gog, pinnedHeight 41, pinnedBottom 41 and listY 41, with contentHeight 172 equal to height 172, so the fitting list has no scroll range.

Observed in the live capture: the freshness text, the refresh glyph and the ? button read as one ink. No layout or colour code changed since the change that unified them, so this is a visual re-check rather than a fresh measurement.

A toast fired through the real notificationArgs argv appeared with the Loot Drops app name and chest glyph, and clicking it opened the panel on the live desktop. The click action is omarchy-shell -q salmun-nister.loot-drops open, which is also what the per-widget open handler answers. A test asserts the argv carries no URL at all.

Steam search/results returned HTTP 200 with 56,736 bytes; Epic freeGamesPromotions returned HTTP 200 with 49,858 bytes; GOG giveaway/api/get returned HTTP 404, which the panel renders as an empty store rather than an error. The harness parsed the same live responses into 2 Steam rows and 2 zero-discount Epic offers.

results.check: Private state file is created and readable
results.detail: ~/.local/state/salmun-nister.loot-drops mode 0700 with seen.json mode 0600, holding per-store id baselines for Steam and Epic. The file was byte-identical before and after the notification test.

results.check: Desktop notification fires for a newly free game
results.detail: The Steam baseline was reduced to a single id and the plugin rescanned so the widget re-read the file, then refresh fetched live: a real desktop notification read 'Fireside Feelings is free on Steam'. The widget holds seen state in memory and persists it on every fetch, so editing seen.json alone does not change what the next fetch compares against; the rescan is what loads the reduced baseline.

results.check: Notification does not repeat for an unchanged list
results.detail: A second refresh against the same list produced no further notification and re-recorded both Steam ids in the baseline.

results.check: Switching a store off stops it and hides it
results.detail: Toggled on the live panel: the GOG section disappeared entirely, and toggling it back restored it. The change persisted to the shell config as gogEnabled, which confirms the switch writes a real setting rather than local UI state.

results.check: Muting a bell keeps the store listed but silent
results.detail: Toggled on the live panel: the store stayed listed with its games and the bell showed crossed out, distinct from a disabled store. Both toggles persisted to the shell config as gogNotify and epicNotify and were restored to true.

results.check: Stale is derived from the refresh interval
results.detail: Stale remains 1.5x refreshMinutes: 45 minutes at the 30-minute floor, 135 at the 90-minute default, 18 hours at the 720 maximum, recomputed from Model.staleAfterMs in this run. Unit-tested across those bounds, including that a single missed poll never reads stale and that an out-of-range interval cannot produce a threshold the settings slider disagrees with.

40 model and helper tests, QML lint against the real Qt qmllint with no errors, the helper behaviour suite, and the offscreen harness all pass. The plugin validator reports VALID and the security pass returns advisory capability findings only: negated sudo prose in SECURITY.md, the .template/blueprint AGENTS.md authoring file, and the installer and package-manager surfaces in docs/SETUP.md. Those are review prompts, not errors, and not a marketplace result.

limitations: GOG's success path is fixture-only. GOG returned 404 during this run as it did last time, so the 200 response shape has still never been observed live.
No vertical bar was observed. The tested bar was horizontal (position top).
The derived stale threshold was recomputed and unit-tested but not observed live. Confirming it needs data 135 minutes old under a 90-minute interval, which was not waited out.

Game rows were not clicked in this run. Rows still hand the URL to xdg-open so the browser picks its own window, but opening a store page and confirming which window received the tab was not re-exercised here; that behaviour was confirmed by the user on a previous run and no code covering it has changed since.

preview.png is the Sunlit Sands panel, cropped from a live capture out to the window border; the other three themes in the README are cropped the same way from the same live panel. Solitude has no top border in its capture because its bar sits flush on the panel. No rendering or layout code changed alongside them, and the live panel captured in this run matches the set: same hero, same four games, same empty GOG row and same footer.
The notification click opens the panel rather than the store page, so the notification path does not cover URL opening; only a panel row does.
The documented install command 'omarchy plugin add <git-url>' was still not exercised. Acceptance used the local symlink that the plugin was already installed through.
The bar widget is loaded once per monitor, and only one monitor was exercised.

omarchy-hyprland-focus-app still selects a window by position in hyprctl's client array rather than focus order. This plugin does not depend on it, but other Omarchy panels and any notification that opens a URL still do. Already reported upstream.
